title: Staging asks for sign-in again after the web app is closed: host its web app beside its API
body:
## Summary

On Staging, a User is asked to sign in again every time the web app is closed and reopened, in the Installed Web App and in an ordinary browser tab. Production is not affected. The cause is hosting, not the session code: Staging's web app is on a `vercel.app` address and its API is on a domain we own, so the two are on different sites and the browser does not send the refresh cookie.

The fix agreed in the design session of 2026-10-13 is to host Staging's web app on cPanel beside its API, on the same site, and to retire Vercel.

## Diagnosis (confirmed)

- A reopened web app has no access token and calls the refresh endpoint. That call succeeds only if the browser sends `refresh_cookie`, which is `SameSite=Lax` and has no `Domain` attribute.
- **Staging:** the operator confirmed `POST …/auth/refresh` returns `401` when Staging is revisited in a desktop browser. The web app is on `vercel.app`; the API is on a subdomain of the operator's domain. A `vercel.app` address is never the same site as anything else.
- **Production:** the operator confirmed sign-in persists. Web and API are `myorganiser.app` and `api.myorganiser.app`, the same site.
- **Local:** both are `localhost`, which is why an emulator run kept its session across a full close.

No change to the session code, the cookie, or "Remember me" is part of this issue.

## Decisions

1. **Same site, everywhere.** The web app and its API are hosted on the same site on every environment, because the session depends on it. This was an unwritten assumption; it becomes a recorded rule.
2. **Staging's web app moves to cPanel**, beside its API, on a subdomain of the same domain. Staging stops being a different kind of host from Production. The address is a `staging` environment setting; the public tree does not name the host (ADR 0056).
3. **Vercel is removed entirely**, in the same change: `vercel.json`, the project-settings sync script, the `VERCEL` branch in `next.config.js`, the CLI pin, the gate's Vercel keys, and the Vercel hosting guide. The README's "Live Demo" points at Production.
4. **Staging deploys once a day**, at 16:00 UTC (2am Sydney in standard time, 3am in daylight time), and on a manual dispatch. It no longer deploys on every green `main`. This covers both halves: the backend upload and the web app.
5. **The scheduled run deploys the newest `main` commit whose CI is green.** If Staging already has that commit, the run skips and stays green. A red or still-running newest commit is not an error. The schedule never rolls Staging back: when Staging holds a newer commit that a dispatch put there, the run skips. When the chosen commit is already uploaded but not running, the run fails without uploading again.
6. **Host Apply is unchanged.** It stays operator-dispatched and backend-only, on both environments. A manual dispatch uploads the backend, applies it, and now also deploys the web app at that commit, so an applied Staging has its web app and API on the same commit. The rule that only a commit Staging has uploaded and Host Applied may be Cut is unchanged, and its guard's logic is unchanged. One consequence follows from it: a scheduled run chooses its commit inside the run, so its name records none, and the guard refuses such an upload. After a scheduled upload, a full dispatch is needed before a Cut; `apply_only` is not enough.
7. **The Staging web bundle goes live without a shell.** SSH on the hosting account is a manual toggle that reverts (ADR 0056, amendment of 2026-09-14), so nothing automatic may need it.
   - The bundle is built and uploaded by FTP with the steps Production's web deploy uses (`yarn package:myorganizer:web`).
   - **Restart by file:** the run uploads `tmp/restart.txt` last, which makes the host restart the app.
   - **Install only when dependencies change:** the run compares the bundle's dependency list with the one on the host. When they differ it uploads, does not restart, and fails with a message saying "Run NPM Install" and "Restart" are owed.
8. **A probe proves the build is live.** After the restart file is uploaded, the run requests the Staging web address until the response comes from the build just uploaded, and fails if that does not happen within a few minutes. The running process must identify itself; static files on disk do not count.
9. **The same-site rule is asserted at deploy time on Staging.** One step compares the parent domains of the web address and the API address and fails the run if they differ. It compares the last two labels of each hostname, which is a rule of thumb and is noted as one.
10. **Production's deploy flow does not change.** It keeps the Release Branch guard, Deploy Approval, and the manual install and restart of its web app. It relies on the written rule in decision 1.
11. **The service worker's headers are set for a host that serves files from disk** (added during delivery). On cPanel, files under `public/` are served by the web server, not by the app, so the `Cache-Control` and `Content-Security-Policy` configured for `/sw.js` never applied there. An operator appends a small block to the host's own `.htaccess` once per environment; the repository keeps that block as a snippet outside `public/` and never ships an `.htaccess`, because the document root is the bundle's `public/` folder and already holds the host's configuration, which an upload would replace. A test refuses an `.htaccess` under `public/`, the Staging probe compares the two headers with the expected values, and a test keeps the copies in step. Production needs the same block appended by hand.

## Considered and rejected

- **A custom domain on the Vercel project.** It fixes the session, but keeps Staging on a different kind of host from Production.
- **The web app joining Host Apply.** Host Apply is operator-dispatched, so the web app could never deploy automatically.
- **Routing the API through the web address** with a rewrite. It changes how every request travels to fix a hosting mismatch.
- **`SameSite=None; Secure` on the cookie.** Safari blocks cross-site cookies regardless, so it would not fix iOS.
- **Giving the web app the refresh token in the response body**, as the Mobile App gets it (ADR 0006). It puts a long-lived token where an injected script can read it.
- **Shipping `node_modules` in the bundle.** The host's Node.js selector manages that folder itself.
- **Uploading automatically and going live by hand.** Staging would usually run an older build than the one uploaded.
- **A runtime same-site check in the backend.** It puts hosting logic in the auth path, and the API does not reliably know its own public address.

## Delivery

1. **Operator, before any code.** Create the Node.js app for the new Staging web address in cPanel. Upload a bundle by hand, run "Run NPM Install" and "Restart" once. Then change `tmp/restart.txt` and confirm the app restarts. Confirm sign-in now survives closing the browser. **If restart-by-file does not work on this host, stop and revisit decision 7.**
2. **One branch, one Pull Request** (`fix/1138-…`), closing this issue:
   - `deploy-staging.yml`: the schedule and dispatch triggers, the newest-green selection, the web job (bundle, FTP, install-on-change, restart file, probe, same-site assertion).
   - The gate and its manifest: `check-deploy-pipeline.mjs`, `check-host-apply-workflow.mjs`, and `docs/deployment/release-pipeline.html`, which must change with the workflow.
   - The two small scripts (dependency comparison, probe) with tests.
   - Docs: the cPanel web and backend hosting guides, the CI/CD process, the Host Apply operator setup, the Drive backup guide, the release Skill, and the README. The Vercel hosting guide is deleted.
   - One new ADR recording decisions 1, 2, 4, 7 and the rejected options; a dated amendment on ADR 0028 and on ADR 0056, which both say Staging deploys on every green `main`.
   - `CONTEXT.md`: the **Staging** entry gains that its web app is hosted beside its backend, on the same site. **Host Apply** stays backend-only; the web restart is not Host Apply.
3. **Operator, after the merge.** Add the new `staging` environment settings (web FTP credentials and directory, the web address, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`). Set the backend's `CORS_ORIGINS`, `APP_FRONTEND_URL` and `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` to the new web address and Host Apply. Dispatch the workflow. The first run against a host with no deploy state fails with "install owed": click "Run NPM Install" and "Restart", dispatch again, and watch the probe pass. Then delete the Vercel project and its three secrets, and move the Google OAuth JavaScript origin and the YouTube redirect URI to the new address.
4. **Close-out.** On a real iPhone and a real Android phone, sign in to the Installed Web App on Staging, close it fully, reopen it: it lands on the dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On Staging, signing in, closing the browser or the Installed Web App fully, and reopening lands on the dashboard without asking for sign-in, on a real iPhone and a real Android phone. Logging out still ends the session.
- [ ] The Staging workflow runs on the daily schedule and on dispatch, and not on a push to `main`.
- [ ] A scheduled run deploys the newest green `main` commit, and skips when Staging already has it.
- [ ] A run is green only when the probe has seen the uploaded build answering.
- [ ] A changed dependency list fails the run with the instruction to install and restart.
- [ ] A web address and API address on different parent domains fail the run.
- [ ] No Vercel configuration, code, gate key, or doc remains; `yarn gates:run` passes.
- [ ] The Cut guard still passes for a commit that a dispatch has uploaded and Host Applied.
- [ ] The new ADR, the two amendments and the glossary edit are in the Pull Request.

## Verified on the host (2026-10-13)

- Sign-in survives closing the browser once the web app is on the same site as its API.
- Changing `tmp/restart.txt` restarts the app: the served build changed with no click.
- The running process identifies its build in the page it returns.

## Not verified yet

- Whether the host honours the appended header block for `/sw.js`, and keeps it when it rewrites its own blocks; the probe fails if it does not.
- Whether the host restarts an idle app by itself, which matters only in the window after an upload that owes an install.
- Whether GitHub schedules can follow a timezone; the design assumes they cannot.

## Affected

`.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml`, `tools/scripts/` (deploy pipeline and Host Apply workflow gates, the Vercel sync script, two new scripts), `docs/deployment/`, `docs/adr/`, `CONTEXT.md`, `README.md`, `vercel.json`, `apps/myorganizer/next.config.js`, `package.json`, `.yarnrc.yml`. No library under `libs/` changes.

<details>
<summary>Original report</summary>

## One-line Task Title

The Installed Web App asks for sign-in again every time it is closed and reopened

## Why this issue?

Found by the operator on staging, on physical devices, while running QA Plan #1124 (PRD #1114, PR #1123, merged 2026-10-13). Everything else in the plan passed. This needs its own issue and its own Pull Request.

## Issue Type

Bug Fix

## What it fixes (if bug fix)?

Steps to reproduce:

1. On staging, open the Installed Web App and sign in.
2. Close the app.
3. Open it again.

Expected: still signed in. The vault may ask for its passphrase; that is separate and correct.

Actual: the sign-in page, every time.

What the code does today (read from the source, not yet traced on staging):

- "Remember me" defaults to unchecked. Unchecked stores the access token in `sessionStorage`; checked stores it in `localStorage` (`auth-session-storage-adapter.ts`). The access token lives 10 minutes (`ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES`).
- The user record is always in `localStorage`. On a cold start with no access token, `getSnapshot()` is `restorable` and `restoreSession()` calls the refresh endpoint. If that fails, it clears the session and the guard redirects to `/login`.
- The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie named `refresh_cookie`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` in production, with a 7-day expiry (`cookieHelper.ts`).

So a reopened app stays signed in only if the refresh call succeeds, and that needs the browser to send `refresh_cookie` to the API.

Leading hypothesis (NOT confirmed): on staging the web app and the API are on different sites (the frontend is a Vercel project; the API is hosted elsewhere), so `refresh_cookie` is a cross-site cookie. A `SameSite=Lax` cookie is not sent on a cross-site `fetch`, and Safari blocks cross-site cookies outright, so every refresh fails and the User is sent to sign-in. Locally both are `localhost` (same site), which is why an emulator run showed the session surviving a full close. If this is right, production is affected only if its web and API hosts are not the same site.

Other things to rule out:

- Whether iOS discards the standalone app's storage or cookies on close.
- Whether "Remember me" checked changes the result (with it checked, the access token survives a close, but only for 10 minutes).
- Whether the same happens in an ordinary browser tab on staging after closing it. The hypothesis predicts it does.

How to confirm: on staging in a desktop browser, sign in, close the tab, reopen. In DevTools, check whether the `POST .../auth/refresh` request carries a `Cookie` header and what it returns.

Decision needed before a fix: if it is the cross-site cookie, the options are to serve the API from the same site as the web app on every environment (or proxy `/api` through the web origin), or to change the cookie to `SameSite=None; Secure` (Safari still blocks cross-site, so this would not fix iOS). The "Remember me" default and the 10-minute token life may also need revisiting for an installed app.

This touches auth and session, so it follows `.agents/skills/auth-session-workflow/SKILL.md`.

Acceptance criteria:

- On staging and production, on a real iPhone and a real Android phone, signing in to the Installed Web App, closing it fully, and reopening it lands on the dashboard without asking for sign-in, for the refresh token's lifetime.
- The same holds for a browser tab.
- Logging out still ends the session.
- The cause is recorded in the issue with evidence from the refresh request.
- A test covers a cold start with a stored user and no access token.

## What new feature will it include (if feature addition)?

N/A

## What can it affect (if small change or modification)?

Auth and session restore in `libs/auth` (`src/lib/auth-session-module.ts`, `src/lib/auth-session-storage-adapter.ts`, `src/lib/guard-orchestration.ts`). The "Remember me" checkbox on `apps/myorganizer/src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`. Backend refresh cookie and token lifetimes (`apps/backend/src/helpers/cookieHelper.ts`, `apps/backend/src/helpers/tokenLifetimes.ts`). Any change to cookie `SameSite`/`Secure` or API hosting affects every environment, not only the Installed Web App.

## Which library will be affected by this change?

- libs/auth (`src/lib/auth-session-module.ts`, `src/lib/auth-session-storage-adapter.ts`, `src/lib/guard-orchestration.ts`)
- apps/myorganizer `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` (the "Remember me" checkbox)
- backend `apps/backend/src/helpers/cookieHelper.ts` and `apps/backend/src/helpers/tokenLifetimes.ts`

## Which project is this change focused on?

Frontend / Backend API

## Does this issue require extra attachments or screenshots?

None


</details>
